clue.text: Send little Ernest to the back door

parts.note: to send a letter is to post it

indicators.note: a little Ernest is a shortened one, so the name loses its last letters

parts.note: the man's name Ernest, written out in full

explanation.surface: Someone instructs that young Ernest be packed off to the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' trims the name: a small Ernest loses its final three letters, a common crossword way of shortening a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small secondary gate or rear entrance, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Stoneworker's assistant taking five for debt to court number 4

parts.note: PA is short for personal assistant
V is the Roman numeral for five
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

indicators.note: letter number 4 of the word court is picked out, counting from its start

explanation.surface: A mason's helper takes five days off and gets taken to court over money owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number 4' takes the fourth letter of 'court', R. The 's after Stoneworker stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paviour lays paving stones, a kind of workman in stone.

clue.text: One chap hides in shell-case in the desert

indicators.note: something that hides in another thing sits within it, so one group goes inside the other
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: one can be written as A, the indefinite article
a chap is a man, referred to as he

explanation.surface: A man takes cover inside an empty shell casing out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shell-case' gives the first and last letters of SHELL, S and L, around A HE. The Sahel is the semi-arid belt along the southern edge of the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahel is a dry region of Africa bordering the Sahara, so it is a stretch of arid land.

clue.text: Surrounded by theatre seats during the finale

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a finale is the end of a show
the circle is an upper tier of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: Sitting in the theatre circle, someone feels hemmed in as the show ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The British theatre 'circle' is a raised balcony tier of seats; 'during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be encircled is to be ringed on all sides, completely hemmed in.

clue.text: A large petrel to be found in cornell, Yale too

indicators.note: the word is lurking within the run of letters cornell, Yale and can be found there

explanation.surface: A big seabird turns up at two American Ivy League universities.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is spelt out across 'cornell, Yale'; the lower-case 'cornell' is how the clue is held.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelly is a name for the giant petrel, a large southern seabird.

clue.text: Extreme right-winger's pawn and I leave pacifists in disarray

indicators.note: the pawn and the I leave, so their letters come out of the pool
something in disarray is jumbled, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word pacifists as written, whose letters form the pool
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: An extremist describes peace campaigners being thrown into confusion as some of them walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P and I out of PACIFISTS ('leave') and rearrange the rest ('in disarray'). The 's after right-winger stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascist holds authoritarian far-right views, the extreme of the political right.

clue.text: Rural businesses offering a meal and a date at the main house

parts.note: farms are businesses in the countryside
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: Country enterprises offer visitors dinner and a romantic evening at the big house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can be a meal in its own right, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmstead is a farm's chief dwelling together with its buildings, the principal home on the holding.

clue.text: Gee! Is this a complicated takeover campaign?

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at how intricate a hostile takeover bid has become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges GEE and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege is a sustained military operation to capture a place, so a campaign to take it over.

clue.text: Tool's the devil to use! (Bewail aloud)

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for bewail gives a sound spelt differently

parts.note: to bewail is to lament

explanation.surface: Someone groans about a tool that is a nightmare to use.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMENT spoken gives the -LEMENT ending. 'to use' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a utensil or instrument, a device used for a job.

clue.text: Staggers like a swimmer in a back street

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so it goes inside
back means the abbreviation for street is read in the other direction

parts.note: an otter is a swimming mammal

explanation.surface: Someone lurches along like a swimmer down a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round, and 'in' puts the swimming animal inside it; 'like a' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, as if about to fall.

clue.text: Concerning the car, I've a lurch (wobble)

indicators.note: a wobble shakes things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver admits the car is lurching and wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobble' rearranges the nine letters of I'VE A LURCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicular means relating to vehicles such as cars.

clue.text: Englishman abroad — former hit-man?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a pat is a light hit, and Pat is also a man's name

explanation.surface: An Englishman living overseas is suspected of once being a contract killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-man' looks like a killer, but it gives PAT, both a tap and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat lives outside their native country, like a Briton settled abroad.

clue.text: He looks the wrong way when women are around

definitions.text: He looks the wrong way when women are around

parts.words: He looks the wrong way when women are around
parts.note: describes a man staring at women in an improper manner, not one facing the wrong direction

explanation.definitionFit: An ogler is someone who stares lecherously, looking at women in an offensive way.

clue.text: The way they used to put it last night

definitions.text: The way they used to put it last night

parts.words: The way they used to put it last night
parts.note: an old-fashioned, archaic way of saying the evening just gone

explanation.definitionFit: Yestereve is a poetic, archaic word for yesterday evening.

clue.text: Criticise imported alien a lot initially; I eventually hit back

indicators.note: something imported is brought in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to rate is an old word for scold or criticise

indicators.note: eventually means coming last, so the letter I is placed at the end of the inserted group

parts.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial alien

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of the words a and lot

explanation.surface: An anti-immigrant complaint, with the speaker finally lashing out.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE, meaning to scold, is an old sense; 'imported' places the alien, the initials and finally I inside it, between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to respond to an attack in kind, striking in return.

clue.text: Ordeal for nine assorted prisoners, held every 3 years

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are prisoners of the other word, held inside it

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal

indicators.note: assorted means mixed, so the letters of nine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nine mixed inmates face an ordeal that recurs every three years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' scrambles the number, and 'prisoners' says those letters are held captive inside the ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial events recur once in each three-year period.

clue.text: French friend takes daughter to see boats in their centre

parts.note: ami is French for friend
ships are boats

explanation.surface: A French friend brings their daughter to look at the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to the boats, so the definition means midway along a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle part of a vessel, between bow and stern.

clue.text: Gang of sailors and journalists?

explanation.definitionFit: A press gang forcibly recruited men as sailors; the press also collectively means newspapers and reporters.

clue.text: Though terribly puny, I race around for money

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters are thrown into disorder
around suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Despite being feeble, someone runs a race in hope of a cash prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' and 'around' both signal rearranging PUNY I RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecuniary means relating to money or finance.

clue.text: Quietly told stories as one worked steadily

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to tell stories is to lie

explanation.surface: Someone spun fibs softly while getting on with their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it diligently.

clue.text: Image of old Scotsman on the river

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A portrait of an ancient Scot by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts the first piece above the second. The Ure is a common crossword river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a visual representation, such as a painting or photo.

clue.text: India in charge, leading to a set-back with shows

indicators.note: set-back reads the word set in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: India, as the authority, suffers a defeat in its displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' looks like a reverse, a misfortune, but it tells you to read the word set the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or demonstrate something.

clue.text: Nip back in broken sled for a pin

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other
a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of sled are rearranged
back means the word Nip is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Someone dashes back to a smashed sledge to fetch a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns Nip round, 'broken' scrambles the sledge word, and 'in' puts the first inside the second, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a slender rod or pin on which something turns.

clue.text: Catholic soon is journalist and dubbed saintly

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A Catholic reporter is shortly to be proclaimed a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To be canonised is to be officially declared a saint by the church.

clue.text: Detects small numbers who get points

parts.note: No. is the abbreviated form of number, so its plural is the small form
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Some people sniff out how few are scoring points.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who noses something out detects it by searching or sniffing.

clue.text: Taken for a ride, and chucked out without money

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: dumped means thrown away

explanation.surface: Someone conned and then thrown out penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: To be duped is to be tricked or fooled.

clue.text: Turn round a minute when a new girl appears

indicators.note: turn suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is a circle, the letter O

explanation.surface: Wait a minute, a new girl has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' rearranges O, A and MIN. 'when a new' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, as in the biblical mother-in-law of Ruth.

clue.text: Circle a measure of cereal

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Circle a measure of cereal (5)': O (circle) + A leaves TEN, and no clue word gives TEN or T + EN; the clue seems misheld or the measure unaccounted for.

clue.text: Singletons exploring Tunis

indicators.note: exploring the word moves around its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Single people on a trip around the Tunisian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploring' rearranges TUNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are single things or individual quantities, each counted as one.

clue.text: Yours truly is settled, well stuck in!

parts.note: yours truly means the speaker, so yours truly is gives I'm
planted means settled firmly in place

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are comfortably settled and well established.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is the speaker, so 'Yours truly is' is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implanted is fixed firmly in place, embedded deep.

clue.text: Recruits roll in from three directions

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: E, N and S are three compass directions
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: New soldiers sign up, streaming in from every quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LIST inside E, N and S: E-N-LIST-S.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up, especially for the armed forces.

clue.text: A leading woman, accomplished and full of desire

indicators.note: a word full of another holds it inside

parts.note: something accomplished is done
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A star actress, skilled and brimming with ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' is the container signal; yen as desire comes from the Chinese word for craving.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or senior woman in a field.
